name: Remembering the Lord at the hour of death
method_summary: At the time of the end, leave the body remembering the Lord alone (8.5). Because one goes to whatever state one remembers at the end, as one has habitually dwelt on it, remember him at all times — for Arjuna, while fighting — with mind and intellect offered to him (8.6–7). The yogin's form: with unmoving mind, devotion and yoga-power, breath between the brows (8.10); or with the gates restrained, mind in the heart, breath in the head, uttering Oṃ (8.12–13).
prerequisites: lifelong constant remembrance (8.6–7, 8.14); knowing the Lord with adhibhūta, adhidaiva, adhiyajña (7.30)
signs_of_progress: result stated: one comes to the Lord's state / the supreme goal, without doubt (8.5, 8.7, 8.13)

name: The yogin's departure at death (BhG 8.10–13)
method_summary: As the text states it: at the time of departure, with an unmoving mind, yoked with devotion and by the power of yoga, the yogin makes the breath (prāṇa) enter fully between the brows (8.10); restraining all the gates, confining the mind in the heart, placing the breath in the head, established in yogic concentration (yoga-dhāraṇā), uttering Oṃ, the one-syllabled Brahman, and remembering the Lord, he abandons the body (8.12–13).
prerequisites: the yoga of repeated practice and constant remembrance (8.8, 8.14)
signs_of_progress: result stated: he reaches the supreme divine Person / the supreme goal (8.10, 8.13)
notes: The text gives no further method, duration or warnings; none are added here.

name: Constant remembrance of the Lord (smaraṇa)
method_summary: Remember the Lord at all times, with mind and intellect offered to him, even while doing one's duty (8.7); with a mind yoked by repeated practice and not straying, meditate on the supreme divine Person (8.8); remember him constantly, day after day, with the mind on nothing else (8.14); think of him with no other object (9.22); be one whose mind is on him (9.34).
signs_of_progress: he becomes easy to reach (8.14); he carries the devotee's welfare (9.22); one comes to him (8.7, 9.34)

name: Undivided devotion (ananya-bhakti)
method_summary: Worship the Lord with the mind on nothing else (ananya-cetas, ananya-manas, ananya-bhāk), constantly (8.14, 9.13, 9.22, 9.30); by such devotion the supreme Person is gained (8.22).
signs_of_progress: stated results: the Lord is easy to reach (8.14); he carries their welfare (9.22); even one of very bad conduct is to be counted good, quickly becomes righteous and attains lasting peace; the devotee does not perish (9.30–31)

name: Singing the Lord's names (kīrtana, nāma-saṅkīrtana)
method_summary: The great-souled always glorify the Lord (kīrtayantaḥ), striving, firm in vows, bowing with devotion, ever yoked (9.14).

name: Bowing to the Lord (namaskāra)
method_summary: Bow to the Lord with devotion (namasyantaḥ, 9.14); 'bow to me' (māṃ namaskuru) as part of the closing injunction together with fixing the mind on him, being his devotee and worshipping him (9.34).
signs_of_progress: result stated with 9.34: 'you will come to me alone'

name: The sacrifice of knowledge (jñāna-yajña)
method_summary: Some worship the Lord by sacrificing with the sacrifice of knowledge — as one, as distinct, in many ways — him who faces in all directions (9.15).
notes: Chapter 9 names the practice without further method; its other Gītā occurrences lie outside this chunk.

name: Offering a leaf, flower, fruit or water with devotion
method_summary: Offer the Lord with devotion a leaf, a flower, a fruit or water; what is so offered by one whose self is pure/controlled he partakes of (9.26).

name: Offering all actions to the Lord (mad-arpaṇa)
method_summary: Whatever you do, eat, offer in sacrifice, give or practise as austerity, do it as an offering to the Lord (9.27); mind and intellect offered to him (8.7).
signs_of_progress: result stated: freedom from the bonds of action with good and bad fruits; yoked in the yoga of renunciation, freed, one comes to him (9.28)

name: Surrender (prapatti / śaraṇāgati)
method_summary: Take refuge in the Lord alone (mām eva prapadyante, 7.14; vyapāśritya, 9.32).
signs_of_progress: stated results: crossing the Lord's māyā (7.14); reaching the highest goal, for anyone who takes refuge (9.32)

name: Fixing the gaze or breath between the eyebrows (bhrū-madhya)
method_summary: At departure the yogin makes the breath (prāṇa) enter fully between the brows (bhruvor madhye), with unmoving mind, devotion and yoga-power (8.10).

name: Practice (abhyāsa)
method_summary: The yoga of repeated practice (abhyāsa-yoga): with the mind yoked by it and not straying elsewhere, meditate constantly on the supreme divine Person (8.8).
signs_of_progress: result stated: one goes to the supreme divine Person (8.8)

name: Vedic studentship (brahmacarya)
method_summary: Those who desire the imperishable practise brahmacarya (8.11).
notes: Named only as the discipline of those seeking the imperishable; no method given in this chunk.

name: Concentration (dhāraṇā)
method_summary: 'Established in yoga-dhāraṇā': restraining all the gates, confining the mind in the heart and placing the breath in the head at departure (8.12).

name: Meditation on Om (praṇava-upāsanā)
method_summary: Uttering 'Oṃ, the one-syllabled Brahman' while remembering the Lord as one leaves the body (8.13).
